chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from one who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who borrowed a garment, then went to it and pledged it as collateral, so the owners of the goods came to their goods, and he said: 'They take their goods.'

key_terms.اسْتَعَارَ: borrowed (took as a loan for use)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person borrows an item and then pledges it to someone else?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the right of the original owner (*mudayyir*) to reclaim their specific borrowed item (*arriyah*) supersedes the creditor's claim, as the borrower only held temporary possession. This ruling underscores the principle that pledging an item one does not fully own is valid but subordinate to the owner's right of reclamation, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding *amanah* (trust) and *rahn* (pledge).
